passages.text: Dasylirion acrotrichum, the great desert spoon and green sotol (also, spoon yucca, though not a true Yucca), is a plant native to the Chihuahuan Desert and other xeric habitats in northern and central Mexico.

Description
The foliage is firm narrow bladed leaves up to {{convert|40|in|m}} long, grasslike and {{convert|0.4|in|cm}} across, symmetrically radiating in a rosette, {{convert|6|ft|m}} tall by the same in diameter, from a central core that elongates into decumbent trunks. The mid Summer flower spike of small white flowers is {{convert|6|to|15|ft|m|abbr=off}} tall.

Cultivation
The drought-tolerant and dramatic plant is cultivated by nurseries for use in personal gardens and larger xeriscape landscape projects in the Southwestern United States and California. Dasylirion acrotrichum is hardy to {{convert|20|°F|°C|abbr=on}}
